topic: Forces in climb, Excess power, max angle, maximum rate, Economical climb, time to climb
syllabus_extract: Forces in climb, Excess power, max angle, maximum rate, Economical climb, time to climb.
specific_objectives: 6.1.3.1 Trainee will be able to describe flight performance of aircraft.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of climb performance charts; Instructor supervision required for chart interpretation.
intro_questions: What are the four primary forces acting on an aircraft in steady flight?
How does the relationship between thrust and drag change during a climb?
Define excess power in the context of aircraft performance.

development.content:
Forces acting during climb
Excess power definition
Maximum angle of climb
Maximum rate of climb
Economical climb speed

Time to climb calculation
Performance chart analysis
Practical chart review
Safety precautions
Instructor supervision

Summary of climb performance
Key performance parameters
Operational implications
Review of objectives
Preparation for descent

summary_questions: Explain the difference between maximum angle of climb and maximum rate of climb.
How is economical climb speed determined for fuel efficiency?
Describe the role of excess power in achieving a climb.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how descent forces differ from climb forces, referencing the next lesson plan on glide range.
